title: Masjid and community
description: What to expect at a masjid, how to ask for help, and how to find healthy community.

sections.heading: What a masjid is for
sections.content: A masjid is a place for prayer, learning, community, and service. Many also run classes, youth programs, food drives, new Muslim support, and counseling referrals. Every masjid has its own culture and its own capacity, so one visit tells you about that masjid rather than about Muslims generally.

sections.heading: First visit etiquette
sections.content:
Keep the basics simple:

- Dress cleanly and modestly.
- Take your shoes off where others do.
- Keep your phone quiet.
- Ask where to go if you are unsure.
- Follow the congregation during prayer as best you can.

If you get something wrong, do not panic. People are usually glad to help once they know you are new.

sections.heading: Finding a mentor
sections.content:
A good mentor is patient, reliable, and respectful of your pace. They help with prayer, purification, Quran, community, and everyday questions, without pushing you to change everything at once.

Ask the imam, the office, or a trusted community member: **Do you have someone who helps new Muslims learn the basics?**

sections.heading: Signs of healthy community
sections.content: Healthy community makes Islam more livable. Look for people who encourage prayer, mercy, honesty, family ties, and steady learning. Be careful around people who isolate you, shame you constantly, demand secrecy, pressure you toward marriage, or treat their own culture as the whole religion.
